is §21.8 L26, quoted in the lane brief; this checkout's decision table ends at
L25, so no fetch or reconstruction of the lead's decision record was needed.

### R1: the implemented verdict and preserved bounds

An abstract value and each write fact now carry separate **data** and **control**
bits. Every non-initializing write must have READ data, optionally AMBIENT,
without ARGUMENT or UNKNOWN data. At least one write must supply read evidence.
Literal inserts/defaults retain the existing identity exception. Conditions,
loop bounds/exits, sort/group keys and slice/element positions contribute control;
that control does not disqualify the written data. Arithmetic combines operand
data and preserves their control separately. A copied argument field remains
ARGUMENT even after sorting, slicing, grouping or shaping. Unknown constructs
still add UNKNOWN data: moving an unsupported condition into the control channel
does not make its dependence known. The same audience, unconditional-rule,
immutable, append-only, maintain-target and native-writer checks still apply.

The previous journal's audit remains the history; these are its changed entries:

| Previous audit entries | L26 model |
| --- | --- |
| `If`, statement branches, return guards, loop bounds, `break`/`continue` | Join candidate data; record the selector in control, including helper writes and cached write replay. |
| `Shape` / `ShapeUse`, field and element projection | Preserve projected field data; carry source/element selection separately through nested fields. An unrelated argument field never becomes copied data. |
| `Sort`, `Group`, `Slice`, `First`, `Last`, `At` | Keys and positions select values through control. A group's `key` remains the original key's data; sorting never erases supplied field data. Unknown key forms remain UNKNOWN. |
| `Count` over a represented list | Use its cardinality provenance, not the union of fields in its elements. A literal list's length is ambient; a read list's cardinality is read-derived. Text/opaque-input count retains its input summary. |
| `Sum` and scalar arithmetic/builtins | Combine consumed data and preserve control. Projected sum includes source cardinality and projection data. Min/max/sorted/divmod retain the conservative operand union. |
| Loop-carried addition/subtraction | A direct carried `n = n + ...` / `n = n - ...` consumes read cardinality. A new local, a reset binding, an unrelated constant assignment or a constant helper called per row does not gain READ. Other unrepresented recurrences retain their conservative summaries. |
| `Write` | Record data and control separately; control never manufactures READ evidence. The representative expression includes parentheses around a conditional arithmetic operand. |

Every other audit entry and the UNKNOWN fallback are retained. The abstract
representation still shares values; the **4,096 expanded-node**, **128 value
level**, **262,144 weighted catalog work unit** and **128 traversal frame**
bounds are unchanged. Control has one shared selector witness per summary;
column diagnostics retain at most two representative selected expressions.
Helper cache keys include control. Function-local accumulators do not inherit
an enclosing caller loop's cardinality. Neither the core meter nor admission,
IR, value serialization, engine execution or a conformance case changed.

### R2: every inverted case and the silent controls

All renamed tests state why the former silent verdict flips:

| Final positive test | Flipped cases / reason |
| --- | --- |
| `l26_conditional_delta_is_control_and_toggle_message_names_both_arms` | Moves the former `conditional argument` silent case out of `argument_or_ambient_writer_disqualifies_across_the_catalog`: `p.score + (1 if value else -1)` consumes a read and ambient delta. Also pins the exact statement-toggle message with `liked` in `setLike`. |
| `l26_slice_positions_choose_ambient_deltas_without_supplying_data` | Scalar, nested-object and nested-list picks from `[1, -1]`; `offset` selects an ambient delta added to a read. |
| `l26_break_chooses_how_many_read_values_are_summed` | Break after accumulation, directly and under a read-dependent outer condition; `choice` selects how many `row.score` values are summed. |
| `l26_statement_helper_and_loop_control_choose_read_derived_writes` | Statement ±1 arms, helper cache, loop branch, argument loop count, break after write, cached helper before break, expression helper, short-circuit helper, guarded-return helper: all write read-derived data selected by control. |
| `l26_sort_and_group_keys_choose_elements_without_supplying_their_fields` | Ascending first, descending last, indexed pick, descending nested field, multiple sort keys, nested grouped item, group count and projected group sum; argument keys select, while delta data stays ambient and is added to a read. |
| `l26_statement_constants_and_loop_counts_choose_deltas_without_supplying_data` | Constants chosen by a statement, argument-bounded count, break before accumulation, helper loop return choosing 1/2; chosen deltas do not supply argument data. |
| `l26_optional_shape_presence_selects_a_read_derived_field` | Inline and named optional shapes move out of the unknown-forms silent test: caller chooses presence, projected data comes from a read. Unknown-table and rule-only `created` cases remain silent. |

`l26_control_alone_does_not_manufacture_read_data` and
`l26_a_constant_helper_called_in_a_read_loop_has_no_read_data` pin the converse:
read conditions, repeated constant assignment, per-iteration reset/local
increment, sort keys and an ambient helper cannot manufacture read data.
`l26_selected_argument_fields_still_supply_data` pairs silent direct arguments,
arithmetic, copied object/shape fields, sorted/sliced payloads and copied group
keys with positive read replacements. All ten `l26_` tests are red on the exact
base and green on the candidate, including the positive companions of silent
argument cases. The malformed-call no-panic and bounded/widened-value tests
remain green.

The existing silent controls are retained. `score: amount`, `p.score + amount`
and argument fields (including helper/shape/write-result fields) carry ARGUMENT
data. `editedAt: now`, `done: true` and `lastSeen: now` are ambient-only.
`messages.ordinal` is immutable; the ordinal/readOrdinal fixture's insert and
update rules additionally name `.principal = viewer`. A `readOrdinal` bump is
silent because of that restricted rule; its unrestricted companion takes the
caller's ordinal, which supplies ARGUMENT data. The append-only ordinal test
uses the IR's AppendOnly constraint (Quarry has no spelling) and verifies that
removing it would note the derivation. Job-written totals under `deny` have no
unconditional write rule. Maintain targets are excluded. Widened recursive
values and exhausted catalogs retain UNKNOWN and stay silent.

This is the fifth W15b entry, appended on `sb4/w15b-land` over exact base

The round-three brief requests these four findings only and explicitly replaces
the full-suite instruction with the language, documentation and reference checks.
Nothing is committed, pushed, tagged or published by this lane.

- **F12:** an upsert's returned id preserves the supplied key's data bits.
  Named `id` keys and a sole positional byId candidate retain ARGUMENT or READ;
  ambiguous positional candidates retain UNKNOWN. An id minted without an id
  key stays AMBIENT. The id is carried on the abstract returned object, without
  creating a declared-column write fact for the implicit id. The caller's
  mixed-object example now stays silent, including a helper result returned
  from the cache. A read-supplied id still qualifies, both alone and beside
  another read; a minted id alone is silent but combines with a read as AMBIENT.
- **F13:** the choice witness uses sorted argument names in the current program
  or helper scope instead of the whole condition string. `set and not exists
  likes[postId, viewer]` and `not set` therefore name both stored expressions.
  A second regression uses `enabled` and `set` in different condition orders.
  The existing shared-condition and expression-toggle test is retained. The
  bounded name walk skips read-key selectors and falls back to “an argument”
  when it cannot name a direct parameter; it changes no data/control bit rule.
- **F14:** non-numeric copies lead with the source-pinning rule. Maintains can
  produce int, decimal and money values here, so those types keep the existing
  maintain advice. Tests cover nullable principal, text, bool, time and JSON
  copies, plus all three supported numeric types. The feeds card explains the
  distinction and supplied-id provenance; the code's `why` blurb includes L26's
  selector sentence. The package README is byte-for-byte unchanged.
- **F15:** the helper-mediated carried increment remains a conservative miss,
  as instructed. The new ignored test asserts the desired one-note result,
  after proving that the equivalent direct addition already emits one note.
  Its exact ignore reason is `F15: helper-mediated carried increments do not
  yet receive READ cardinality evidence`. This preserves a failing executable
  description of the gap rather than making current silence the desired result.

What I learned: an id filled by an upsert key is written data, even though the
same id spelling is ambient when minted. Conversely, a selector's diagnostic
identity should describe the argument choosing the data, not its entire guard.
The repair remains entirely in the optional note pass and its published help:
no binder acceptance, IR, engine, value serialization, charge or ceiling changes.
The existing LLP 3000.007 §21.8 L26 annotation still governs the bit rule.

## 2026-09-20 — W15b-6: cardinality is provenance of its own (F16–F18)

Continued `sb4/w15b-land` at `13ed112a257182bdf58c6e42141cdb7defd644aa`,
without committing. This sixth lane entry implements L28 from the lead's
2026-09-20 brief, amending L26 under [LLP 3000.007 §21.8](../llp/3000.007-relaxed-quarry-and-explicit-residency.rfc.md#21.8).
The lead owns the L28 row itself; this lane does not edit §21.8. The Snapback 4
fence, simulator invariants and execution decisions remain those of
[LLP 3000 §6–§7](../llp/3000-snapback4.explainer.md#6-the-simulators-invariants).
The optional note still changes no admitted program, IR, engine execution,
serialized value, charge, ceiling or existing conformance case.

### F16: data, cardinality and control

Collections now have an explicit cardinality field, separate from their item
tree's data and from control. A list parameter's items and cardinality are
ARGUMENT; a read page's cardinality is READ, independently of the fields its
shape keeps; a literal array's cardinality is AMBIENT. Nested list parameters
and stored list columns retain the same distinction at each level. The field
participates in structural equality, widening and helper-cache keys. It is
included when a whole collection is consumed or written, not copied into every
item merely because that item is visited by a loop or shape.

`count` consumes the cardinality, including the `Len` lowering of `count(text)`;
Quarry still has no `len` alias. A SHA-256 string's length is AMBIENT (64), while
its content retains its input's data. `sum`, projected sum and first/last/at
consume item data together with cardinality. Min/max and the `sorted` pair keep
both candidates' item trees and cardinalities, with conservative operand unions
on consumed data. Shape, slice, sort and group retain source cardinality; group
keys and positions still select finite choices under L26. A read filter may
add its predicate's data bits. `range` and `tokens` now produce actual abstract
lists rather than scalar summaries: their bounds/text supply their cardinality.

Direct carried addition/subtraction and list append consume the loop domain's
cardinality. Thus an argument-sized constant accumulation cannot become a
read-derived value merely by adding `p.score` after the loop. Locals reset on
each iteration and finite choices of constants remain selection. Bounded,
scoped sets of data names follow aliases to recognize a recurrence whose
transfer is not represented; those recurrences become UNKNOWN rather than
silently losing their cardinality. The name sets supply no positive READ or
ARGUMENT evidence. Function-local accumulators do not inherit a caller loop's
cardinality. The ignored F15 positive remains a limitation: helper-mediated
increment over read rows is still silent, now explicitly UNKNOWN.

### F17: complete expression and builtin audit, with cardinality

This table supersedes the earlier audit for the current implementation without
editing its history. “Carried” means the bounded abstraction retains both item
data and cardinality; unions can conservatively retain extra input dependence.
It is not constant folding, path-feasibility analysis or an authorization proof.
Every row becomes UNKNOWN on exhausted work/depth or an oversized value. A
shape-dependent form without a represented source shape is UNKNOWN even when
its scalar summary includes READ. The two channels must both survive before a
form is called carried.

| AST expression | Items / value data | Cardinality | Audit result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Name` | Scoped value; typed list arguments contain ARGUMENT items; viewer/now/commit/new AMBIENT | Scoped field; nested list parameters ARGUMENT | Carried; unresolved name UNKNOWN |
| `Focal` | Current row or list item | Its own nested collection cardinality | Carried |
| `Literal` | AMBIENT, with the existing insert-initializer marker | AMBIENT | Carried |
| `Array` | Field-preserving join of the literal's elements | AMBIENT, independent of the elements | Carried |
| `Object` | Independent fields | Nested fields retain theirs; object field count is AMBIENT | Carried |
| `Unary` | Operand summary; negative literal keeps initialization | Scalar result / text summary; no list produced | Carried |
| `Binary` | Operand union; list append joins element trees; `??` joins candidate values without flattening them | List append joins both cardinalities and consumes its loop domain; coalescing keeps both candidates' fields | Carried; unsupported heterogeneous joins UNKNOWN |
| `Member` | Selected field; stored list fields are typed recursively | Selected field's own cardinality | Carried; an opaque field keeps only a scalar summary, so a later shape becomes UNKNOWN |
| `Call` (helper) | Actual argument values, returned shape and cached write facts; unused helpers get typed ARGUMENT values | Preserved in arguments, results, structural cache keys and write replay | Carried; recursive/malformed/unknown calls UNKNOWN |
| `Read` | Stored row/maintain READ; connected AMBIENT; typed row fields | Explicit/structurally resolved pages READ, plus filter data; opaque stored input length READ | Carried for scalar consumption and resolved shapes; positional point-versus-prefix type ambiguity keeps an opaque summary and a subsequent shape is UNKNOWN |
| `Merge` | Known stored row shape; every lane/prefix/filter expression traversed | READ, plus filter data; lane discovery selects the read population | Carried; unknown source UNKNOWN |
| `Exists` | Read/presence summary | Scalar; prefix existence consumes the read population | Carried |
| `Created` | Rule-only form | UNKNOWN | UNKNOWN, unchanged |
| `Assert` | Successful value unchanged | Unchanged | Carried |
| `Shape` | Projected fields; dropped input fields do not become copied data | Source collection cardinality survives even when every field is replaced | Carried for represented sources; opaque sources and mixed row/list sources UNKNOWN |
| `ShapeUse` | Same projection, including named spreads | Same preservation | Carried for represented sources; missing/recursive/opaque shape UNKNOWN |
| `Walk` | Known stored row, including typed list columns | READ; seed chooses the stored traversal | Carried; unknown table UNKNOWN |
| `If` | Join both result trees; condition stays control | Join both result cardinalities; finite ambient choices stay AMBIENT | Carried; incompatible object/list join UNKNOWN |
| `Write` | Supplied/default/key fields and prior-image summaries; existing id handling unchanged | Supplied list fields retain theirs; opaque omitted prior-image fields require UNKNOWN for a later shape | Carried for represented returned fields; opaque projections UNKNOWN. The separate round-4 update-id finding is not repaired by this cardinality lane |

| Core builtin / Quarry form | Items / value data | Cardinality | Audit result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Calendar` / day, hour, bucket | Supplied scalar-input union | Scalar result | Carried |
| `Len` / count(text) | Returns length provenance | Input length becomes output data | Carried; SHA-256's fixed 64-character length is AMBIENT |
| `Slice` | Base item tree / text data; positions control selection | Base cardinality | Carried |
| `Concat` / list append or text `+` | Both item trees or scalar text-input union | List cardinalities joined; repeated append also consumes domain cardinality | Carried |
| `Lower`, `Trim` | Input text summary | Input data supplies the transformed text length | Carried |
| `Sha256` | Input content summary | AMBIENT fixed length | Carried |
| `Join` | Item data, source cardinality and separator summary | Scalar text length carries the consumed input union | Carried |
| `Group` | Key retains its data; grouped items retain theirs; keys select membership | Both outer groups and inner items preserve source cardinality; a partition of an ambient literal list remains finite selection | Carried; unsupported key UNKNOWN |
| `First`, `Last`, `At` | Selected item recursively consumes source cardinality; index stays control | Any selected nested collection retains its cardinality plus the consumed outer cardinality | Carried |
| `Min`, `Max` | Both possible values/shapes retained with conservative data union | Both cardinalities retained instead of flattening into item data | Carried; heterogeneous shapes UNKNOWN |
| `Divmod` | Both tuple components carry both numeric inputs | Scalar components | Carried |
| `Sort` | Item tree preserved; every literal sort key, including descending keys, stays control | Base cardinality | Carried; unsupported key UNKNOWN |
| `MentionTokens` / tokens | Input text summary as token data | Input text summary as token-count provenance | Carried as a list |
| `DeterministicShare` / share | Amount, recipient data and recipient-list cardinality | Scalar result | Carried |
| `Count` | Returns cardinality, not discarded projected fields | Input cardinality becomes output data | Carried; any UNKNOWN input keeps the fallback |
| `Sum` | Item data plus cardinality; projected sum consumes projection data plus source cardinality | Becomes part of scalar output data | Carried |
| `CountCapped` | Same internal count lowering | Source cardinality | Carried; no separate Quarry spelling |
| `Connected` / connected[p] | AMBIENT presence | Ambient scalar connection count | Carried |
| sorted(a, b) | Both possible component values/shapes | Both candidates' cardinalities survive pair binding | Carried |
| range(a, b) | Both bounds' data in iteration values | Both bounds' data in iteration count | Carried as a loop-domain list |
| Unknown/malformed builtin or unsupported key | UNKNOWN; arguments still traversed for writes | UNKNOWN | UNKNOWN, unchanged |

Statement audit: bindings preserve values and alias data names; branch joins
preserve both provenance fields and keep conditions in control; returns preserve
both fields; expression/emit/require traverse their values and helper writes.
Direct loop-carried addition/subtraction/append consumes the domain cardinality.
Other carried self-dependence (helper calls, arithmetic through aliases,
non-additive recurrence and sorted-pair aliases) is UNKNOWN. Loop exits remain
control and still reach cached writes; constant reassignment and per-iteration
reset do not manufacture READ. Literal insert initialization keeps its exception.

New UNKNOWN demotions are explicitly exercised by
`review_f17_opaque_shapes_and_unmodelled_recurrences_stay_unknown`
(opaque JSON and mixed object/list projection),
`review_f17_implicit_prefix_projection_is_unknown_until_its_collection_shape_is_known`
(type-dependent implicit population shape, paired with the explicit-page positive),
and `review_f17_loop_recurrence_aliases_helpers_and_nonadditive_forms_stay_unknown`
(helper, local alias, multiplication and sorted-pair recurrence over argument and
read domains, paired with the direct read-count positive). Existing unknown
names, rule-only `created`, recursive shapes/calls, malformed arities, unsupported
sort/group keys and budget widening stay unknown with their existing tests.

All existing `l26_` positive test functions remain positive. The one superseded
subcase is named explicitly: `range(0, amount)` followed by a carried constant
increment moved into F16's silent regressions. Its old positive slot now uses
`range(0, p.score)`, and its enclosing test is renamed
`l26_statement_constants_and_read_loop_counts_choose_deltas_without_supplying_data`.
The separate `l26_statement_helper_and_loop_control_choose_read_derived_writes`

## 2026-09-20 — W15b-7: loops prefer silence (F19–F20, L29)

Continued `sb4/w15b-land` at
`5c8ec7cd03dc6e63893d1213f707778d16b4bc07`, without committing.
This seventh lane entry implements the lead's L29 ruling supplied in the
2026-09-20 brief under [LLP 3000.007 §21.8](../llp/3000.007-relaxed-quarry-and-explicit-residency.rfc.md#21.8);
that section remains the lead's and is unchanged here. The governing scope is
[LLP 3000 §6–§7](../llp/3000-snapback4.explainer.md#6-the-simulators-invariants)
and the optional all-writers note in
[LLP 3000.007 §20.21](../llp/3000.007-relaxed-quarry-and-explicit-residency.rfc.md#20.21).
No change to admission, execution, the serialized value model, engine ceilings,
existing corpus cases, or the feeds rule sentence is needed.

### F19: the loop join

The body is walked syntactically once per analyzed loop to collect every
assigned name, recursively through branches and nested loops, without stopping
at a return, break or continue. The traversal and name collection use the
existing depth and work budgets. At each fixed-point join, every collected
binding that survives outside the iteration takes the domain's cardinality
bits into its data and nested fields; a binding not visited before an exit
uses its incoming value. Resets, branch joins and the assignment's position
cannot suppress that union. Unassigned bindings and assignments after the loop
keep their ordinary behavior. Existing unsupported-recurrence UNKNOWN
summaries remain conservative; the join never removes them.

This supersedes the loop precision in the sixth entry's statement audit;
the expression and builtin rows otherwise stand.

| Statement | Items / value data | Cardinality | Audit result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Loop / body join | Every assigned outer binding, including its nested value fields, unions the domain's cardinality regardless of resets, branches, nested loops or exits | ARGUMENT for argument lists/ranges; UNKNOWN for an unknown domain; READ for a read domain; AMBIENT for a literal domain | conservative (L29) |
| Bindings and branch joins outside loops | Existing value/alias propagation and selection control | Existing cardinality preserved | Unchanged |

Four new active test functions cover the exact GPT conditional-reset program,
36 variants (12 assignment shapes × 3 argument domains), an argument loop
nested inside a read loop with a read-domain replacement, and the read-count /
`range(0, p.n)` controls plus outside-loop precision and an unknown domain.
The argument variants include direct accumulation, conditional and unconditional
resets, nested branches and loops, and assignments before and after breaks and
continues. On the base, 33 of the 36 variants emitted a note; after the fix,
all 36 are silent. The exact GPT program changes from 1 note to 0. The
read-domain conditional-reset control changes from 0 to 1; direct read counts
and the existing L26/L28 positive assertions remain noted.

The old read-loop constant-assignment and unconditional-reset subcases were
split out of `l26_control_alone_does_not_manufacture_read_data` into
`l29_unconditional_reset_precision`, with the argument-range unconditional-reset
precision control beside them. This test is explicitly ignored with
`L29: loops prefer silence`. L29 also supersedes the silent expectation in
`l26_a_constant_helper_called_in_a_read_loop_has_no_read_data`, which receives
the same ignore reason: its outer assigned result now takes READ at the join.
Its positive `p.score + delta` assertion remains active in the new F19 controls.
The unrelated non-loop and iteration-local controls stay active. The two
previous ignores (the retained external calibration survey and F15's unsupported
helper-mediated recurrence) are unchanged: 4 ignored tests in total.

The trade is deliberate: an unconditional reset in an argument-bounded loop
can now hide a valid note even though it stores at most one, while a constant
assignment over a read domain takes READ. The pass no longer spends precision
on proving those loop shapes. Nothing here turns the optional note into an
authorization or equality analysis.

## 2026-09-20 — W15b lands after six blind rounds; the last two findings applied under L29's rule

Round 6 (the last, LLP 3000.007 §21.8 L29): Grok READY WITH CHANGES — a caller-supplied seek
bound or `matching` text decides how many rows a page holds, so a count of it is
caller-controlled; GPT NOT READY — a helper named like a syntactic builtin (`divmod`,
`sorted`, `range`) lent its provenance where the binder bypasses it. Both are behavioural, and
L29 says what happens: the construct goes conservative and the lane lands without another
round. The lead applied both directly:

- seek values, `matching` text, the cursor and the filter now enter a page's cardinality
  (READ from the read, ARGUMENT from an argument); a **key** does not — it selects which group,
  whose size is a fact about the data, so `count(likes[postId])` stays the footgun and notes.
  A `matching` page inside a mutation is refused by admission (`E_STRUCTURAL_FANOUT`), so that
  half is defensive; the seek bound is the reachable case.
  `round6_seek_bounds_and_matching_text_shape_a_pages_cardinality_but_keys_only_select`.
- a two-name binding is `divmod`/`sorted` by syntax and `for … in range(a, b)` is syntax: when
  a helper of that name exists the pass now yields UNKNOWN instead of the helper's value.
  `round6_helpers_named_like_syntactic_builtins_are_unknown_where_the_binder_bypasses_them`.

GPT's first attempt at round 6 died in a provider capacity error and was rerun; both records
are verbatim under `llp/reviews/3000.007-w15b-aggregate-provenance*`, twelve in all.

After the two fixes: `cargo test -p snapback4-lang` 353 passed, 0 failed; the retained
calibration survey unchanged (2 / 2 / 4 / 3); docs budget 300/300; ref-check 0 errors.

What six rounds bought, in order: a compiler that cannot panic on a malformed unused helper;
an environment join that is linear and a value that is bounded; three optimistic selections
made honest; **one wrong rule, the lead's** (information flow → data dependence, L26); one
missing provenance axis (cardinality, L28); and the decision that loops prefer silence (L29).
The pass that lands is stated in the terms it computes — data, control, cardinality — and every
construct it does not model precisely is UNKNOWN, which is silence.
## 2026-09-19 — W14a alternative 3: uniform word expansion measurement spike

Uncommitted experiment against `f37e45e7ab059c44b5fe982115e56cc15414bf26`,
with a default-off `W14A_WORD_EXPANSION_METER` compile-time switch in
`engine/read.rs`. Admitted uniform scopes discover past 32 words; generated
lanes now pay a step and descriptor/head heap charges. Non-uniform scopes
retain 32. This is measurement code, not a landing or a complete allocation
audit; the owned scan's general nested IR and transient clones still need
accounting before production use. The detailed record is
[W14A-SPIKE.md](../W14A-SPIKE.md).

At 45 distinct `kx00` through `kx44` words, the base returns 20 rows with
`cut: "words"` and no cursor; the spike returns all 45 in three ordered
pages, with a cursor on both full pages, on server SQLite, device memory,
device SQLite and the actual wasm device under Node 24. At 200 and 1,000
words every host completes in 10 and 50 pages without a cut. Native
first-page counters at 1,000 words are examined 1,000, index entries 1,001,
rule probes 1 on the server / 0 on devices, steps 5,027, heap 4,143,712 B,
output 2,031 B and writes 0. The 9,000-hidden-row paired worlds produce
identical viewer bytes on each host. Wasm does not expose its meter; its
counters were not invented from the native measurements.

Sixty samples after three warm-ups: server first-page p50/p95 changes from
403.083/547.583 to 445.458/602.500 microseconds; the terminal base walk
(only 20 rows) is 431.042/570.916, versus the complete 45-row spike walk
at 1,655.209/1,883.042 microseconds. Shared-host load averages were 36–52;
these are in-process observations, not controlled throughput claims. The
base wasm build is 1,601,169 B raw / 441,568 B gzip, already 7,568 B above
the unchanged 434,000 B budget. The spike is 1,603,020 / 442,202 B, a
1,851 B raw / 634 B gzip increase, and its build also exits over budget.

The positive 45-word regression is red before and green after. Spike

## 2026-09-20 — W14A build: uniform word expansion spends the meter

Implemented revision 2 of `LANE-DESIGN.md` against base
`bef001a27a81412240ab66776e7746ecb82e24a3`. The compile-time spike switch is
removed. An admitted, statically uniform scope discovers words under the
existing meter. An admitted non-uniform scope still retains 32, witnesses
and discards the 33rd, records `word_cut_at`, and keeps its disclosure
class. Device trust alone does not make a scope uniform. Discovery/opening
cuts have no continuation; an established-head drain cut keeps the existing
continuation. A capped heap unwind still returns null/incomplete/meter/no-next.
The final-answer veto, cursor version, serialized values, ceilings, existing
corpus cases, pages/partition and device boundary implementations are unchanged.
The rule's single new reference is LLP 3000.007 §20.24.

Allocation accounting is cumulative interpreter work, not live RSS. Let
`A(n) = 0` for zero bytes, otherwise `max(n, sizeof(usize))`,
`V<T>(n) = A(n * sizeof(T))`, and `B(value)` count owned String/Id/Bytes
bodies and recursive Array slots/bodies; Row/Map/asset clones share an Arc.
Vector/heap growth explicitly uses `reserve_exact`, starts at one slot,
doubles capacity, and charges the full replacement `V<T>(new_capacity)`
before growing. This avoids Vec's implicit four-slot minimum for large
inline scans. Generated scans are boxed once; ordinary scans are borrowed.
All formulas below run before their corresponding interpreter allocation
or retention grows. Existing bounded store fetch temporaries stay at the
Rows boundary; they are not accumulated as discovered descriptors.

| Allocation site | Charge before allocation/retention |
| --- | --- |
| Scope input / WordRead fields | `V<Value>(scope length) + V<String>(field count) + sum A(field.len)`; expression evaluation retains its existing charge |
| Query and row tokenization | ASCII fold `A(input.len)`; non-ASCII NFC/lowercase/wasm bridge scratch `48*A(input.len)`; each unique retained token `A(UTF-8 len)` plus geometric String-vector growth; duplicate/truncated tokens compare borrowed slices first |
| Discovery prefix bound | `A(first term.len)` |
| Discovery key decoding | `2*V<Value>(index components + 1) + 2*A(encoded key.len)` before decoding |
| Discovered word and next seek | `2*A(word.len) + V<Value>(1)` plus geometric retained-word-vector growth |
| Generated merge / lane IR | Exact `V<MergeLane>(word count) + A(site.len)`; each lane pays the complete recursive scan tail, exact prefix-expression slots and cloned scope bodies; the original prefix is replaced without cloning and discarding it |
| Arbitrary IR clones | All Expr/Stmt/Read/Scan/Merge/LoopDomain variants, boxes, vectors, object fields, names, literal bodies and after/before/range/filter expressions; B-tree object fields use the node bound below |
| Cursor suffix / decoding | Exact suffix slots with room for an appended id, copied names and recursive column-type bodies; `8*A(token.len)` for each validation/decode group, including initial merge validation |
| Generated lane opening | One Steps unit before admission; boxed direct-source iterator; generated Scan box; exact evaluated prefix slots; bounds/WordRead owned bodies; geometric retained-descriptor-vector growth |
| Prepared scan / scan cursor | Prefix slot/body clones and all owned bounds; bounds again for the working cursor; singleton positional bounds pay `V<Value>(1)` |
| Row scan decoding / buffers | Same key-decoder scratch as discovery; `A(key.len)` before each raw-key copy; retained row `row.heap_bytes()` plus exact/geometric row/key-vector allocations before retention; Vec-to-VecDeque transfers the buffer |
| Heap heads / refill keys | Geometric `MergeHead` storage; exact suffix Value slots and copied column/id bodies before each head/refill key |
| Dedup / output drain | Each pop pays `11*sizeof((String,())) + 12*sizeof(usize) + 32 + A(id.len)` (one conservative full internal B-tree node, including duplicate attempts); emitted last-key clones pay Value slots/bodies, and output rows pay geometric vector growth |

The range/list `charge_lane` path and its existing descriptor formula are
unchanged. A conservative first attempt used large inline Scan descriptors
and per-column token vectors; it exhausted heap in existing dense controls.
Boxing owned descriptors, borrowing ordinary ones, and tokenizing into one
metered vector eliminated those unnecessary allocations. Unicode, token
truncation, multi-column dedup and the 512-token ceiling match the index
tokenizer in direct positive tests. A nested, untaken 1,000,000-byte cursor
IR expression now reaches the heap cut before any head opens; the small
8-byte expression remains a positive continuation case.

## 2026-09-19 — W14A-BUILD-R1: allocation ledger and disclosure corrections

Continued W14a from `99fdcb6c6a470965f5bc6a0fafa4cf5f8b367647`, the R0/spike
squash rebased onto main `6bc2520963`. This round implements REV3 A–H under
LLP 3000.007 §20.24.1. Nothing was committed, pushed, tagged or published.

Uniform word lanes now borrow their compiled scan/expression trees and share
one scope's remaining terms. Bounds still evaluate per lane, while cursor
validation shares one decoded image. Query tokenization stops at eight terms
at the source. All new interpreter containers grow through prepaid exact
capacities; dedup uses an explicit B-tree root/split bound instead of 80 bytes
per insertion. Cursor construction reserves the largest emitted key, including
a returned-shape rewind, and the later trim-position map is prepaid too.

A finite schema-max-row multiplier cannot cover unbounded IDs/principals.
The narrow Rows store exception therefore charges before owning fetched
images: SQLite first queries byte lengths to reserve native column payload
scratch, then borrows JSON and prices its typed decoder before decoding.
Memory shares row images and prepays result/key copies. Store wrappers forward
the metered method. The optional PostgreSQL adapter preflights lengths in the
existing transaction; it compiled with the feature enabled, but no PostgreSQL
server was used. Existing general expression/rule-probe accounting and the
admitted non-uniform eager traversal retain their prior contracts.

The resource ledger is below. These are cumulative allowances, not RSS;
observed heap totals are not the proof of the bound.

Allocation ledger for uniform, meter-bounded word expansion (LLP 3000.007 §20.24).
Charges accumulate allocations, not live RSS. A failed allowance precedes the
indicated growth. Existing general expression evaluation and rule-probe engines
retain their own accounting; this ledger prices the expansion's added storage.

Notation: A(n)=0 for n=0, otherwise max(n,sizeof(usize)); S<T>(n)=A(n*sizeof(T));
V(v)=S<Value>(len)+owned String/Id/Bytes/Array payload recursively (Arc images 0);
B(b)=V(each vector bound)+owned scalar/word payload. G<T> charges S<T>(max(1,2c))
on replacement of capacity c; ordinary collect growth uses vec_growth<T>.
N<K,V>=11*sizeof(K)+11*sizeof(V)+12*sizeof(usize)+32; insertion at n entries
reserves N*(floor(log2(n+1))+2), one possible split per level and a new root.
R(prefix,bounds)=range(), including key escaping and replacement capacities.
J(json)=stored_row(), an allocation-free count of quoted bytes, typed map roots,
fields, arrays and commas; its formula is implemented in word_heap.rs and tested against allocs.
For JSON length L, typed Row/Map roots O, actual fields F, arrays Q and unquoted
commas C: J=4*A(L)+(O+(F>11 ? 2*floor(F/5) : 0))*N<String,Value>
+(Q=0 ? 0 : 4*S<Value>(4*Q+C))+2*O*S<usize>(1). Cursor construction reserves
2*(S<CursorColumn>(index arity+1)+descriptor+key+8*(256+8*(names+descriptor+key))).

| Site / allocation | Class | Formula | Charge point before growth |
|---|---|---|---|
| Initial field names and scope slots | retained interpreter storage | strings(fields)+S<Value>(scope arity) | discover_words, before to_vec/with_capacity |
| Query normalization/lowercase scratch | bounded store scratch | ASCII A(input bytes); Unicode 48*A(bytes) | tokenize_limit, before fold (also wasm UTF-16 bridge) |
| Query tokens and token vector | retained interpreter storage | A(token bytes)+G<String>, maximum 8 at source | tokenize_limit, before to_owned/reserve_exact |
| Temporary bound singleton vectors | retained interpreter storage | S<Value>(1); evaluated operands use expr accounting | word_bounds, before vec! |
| Cursor validation and cached input | retained interpreter storage | 256*A(token bytes)+A(token bytes), once per distinct token | validate_word_cursor, before decode/reencode/to_owned |
| Cursor suffix names/types/slots | retained interpreter storage | S<CursorColumn>(remaining+id)+names+recursive column payload | suffix, before with_capacity/clone |
| Evaluated cursor bound copies | retained interpreter storage | V(position.values) per lane | word_bounds, before clone |
| Read-table and dependency sets | retained interpreter storage | A(name)+insertion<String,()> only on first insertion | word_note_table, before owned name/insert; dependency traversal borrows rules |
| Visibility and compiled Scan/Expr trees | shared images | 0; borrowed traversal, including eight 4 KiB literals | scan_visibility and merge_lazy never clone per generated lane |
| Scope verdict temporary prefix row/terms | bounded store scratch | verdict(): collect slots+map nodes+names+owned terms+Arc header | discover_words, before prefix_verdict |
| Device coverage diagnostic | retained interpreter storage | 256*(192+V(scope)+A(table)+A(index)+A(site)) | discover_words, before unknown_fact/horizon_coverage |
| Initial discovery bounds.word | retained interpreter storage | A(first term) | discover_words, before clone |
| Store encoded bounds/range endpoints | bounded store scratch | R(prefix,bounds)+copied table/index names | scan_metered, before scan_range and range lookup |
| SQLite native column payload scratch | bounded store scratch | 2*SUM(JSON/key byte lengths)+64*entry count in the same transaction | scalar length preflight, then charge before payload-bearing SQL query; database pages/cached VM are shared images |
| SQLite fetched typed row and key | bounded store scratch | J(borrowed JSON)+A(key bytes)+G<(Value,Vec<u8>)> for each fetched entry | scan_metered, before serde decode/key.to_vec/result reserve |
| Memory fetched key and result slots | bounded store scratch | owned value payload+A(key bytes)+G<(Value,Vec<u8>)> | memory_result, before cloning or reserving |
| Memory row maps; compiled schema/program; SQLite database/cache | shared images | 0 per Arc/borrow; storage engine's existing pages/cache are not interpreter heap | store borrowing; no row-body clone per lane |
| PostgreSQL optional adapter batch | bounded store scratch | 2*R+4096 preflight; 256*SUM(serialized row/key bytes)+vec_growth<(Value,Vec<u8>)>(limit) | scalar preflight then allowance before owning scan result, in same snapshot |
| Every decoded discovery/refill key component | bounded store scratch | 4*S<Value>(max(components,4))+4*A(max(key bytes,8)) | key_decode allowance before key::decode |
| Retained discovered words and after vector | retained interpreter storage | decoded word already paid; 2*A(word)+S<Value>(1)+G<String> | discover_words, before after clone/vector growth |
| Shared fields/remaining terms | retained interpreter storage | S<WordRead>(1)+2*S<usize>(1), payload moved from discovery | merge_lazy, before Rc::new; every lane clones only Rc |
| Lane source iterator | retained interpreter storage | S<Once<Value>>(1) | merge_lazy, before boxed source iterator; no generated scans Vec |
| Per-word evaluated prefix and descriptor | retained interpreter storage | S<Value>(scope+1)+owned scope payload+G<PreparedLane> | merge_lazy, before prefix allocation and descriptor push |
| Range/list descriptor admission | retained interpreter storage | vec_growth<Value>(prefix arity)+G<PreparedLane>; bound copies use the same helpers | merge_lazy, before prefix collection and descriptor push; charge_lane charges only its step |
| Opening/refill prefix and bounds clones | bounded store scratch | V(prefix)+B(bounds), then B(bounds) for scan cursor | word_scan_prepared and scan_prepared, before each clone |
| Every opening/refill fetched batch | bounded store scratch | sum of per-entry store formula, including rejected rows/discarded keys | scan_metered, before each image/key allocation; no post-fetch buffer allowance |
| Optional/default fields or pending-field removal | retained interpreter storage | materialize/object_copy: nodes+owned fields+Arc header+missing-field insertion bounds | before optional materialization / stripping pending |
| Candidate text references | shared images | 0, borrowed iterator (no Vec) | scan_prepared; no tokenizer at all with no remaining terms |
| Complete candidate tokenization | bounded store scratch | same fold/token/G<String> formula, at most 512 retained tokens | tokenize, before folding/copying/growth |
| Filter environment slot | retained interpreter storage | A("$filter")+insertion<String,Value>(env.len) | scan_prepared, before env.insert; row image shared |
| last_rule_visible and returned raw keys | retained interpreter storage | A(key bytes) each; G<Vec<u8>> for result | scan_prepared, before key clone/vector growth |
| Visible-row and drain-page vectors | retained interpreter storage | G<Value> at each replacement | push, before reserve_exact; row image moved/shared |
| Vec to VecDeque buffer transfer | shared images | 0 additional allocation | transfer consumes the existing Vec, never charged twice |
| Merge head key and heap capacity | retained interpreter storage | S<Value>(suffix)+owned component/id payload; G<MergeHead> | charge_word_key and grow, before key construction/heap growth |
| Dedup IDs and B-tree splits | retained interpreter storage | A(id)+insertion<String,()>(seen.len) | merge_lazy, before to_owned/insert |
| Emitted position and moving winning head | retained interpreter storage | V(head.key) for copied last; moving head.key into after is 0 | merge_lazy, before last.clone |
| Repeated meter site strings | retained interpreter storage | A(site) each | before meter.at in admission, opening/refill and filter restoration |
| Shape-cursor map | retained interpreter storage | A(site)+insertion<String,String>; token moved | word_shape_cursor, before record_shape_cursor |
| Page record names/map/position | retained interpreter storage | insertion<String,PagePosition>+3*(A(site)+A(table)+A(index))+2*V(last) | merge_lazy, before record_page |
| Returned shape-position collection | retained interpreter storage | vec_growth<Vec<Value>>(rows)+sum(vec_growth<Value>(suffix)+owned key payload) | merge_lazy, before record_page; generic shaping charge is additional conservative accounting |
| Later returned-shape trim map | retained interpreter storage | sum(A(shape site)+max emitted key bytes+insertion<String,ShapePosition>) over possible shape sites | merge_lazy, before any later trim_shape inserts/clones a position |
| Output cursor construction | bounded store scratch | cursor_build(): 2 descriptors/keys plus JSON/base64 allowance, maximum emitted key (including shape rewind) | merge_lazy, before record_page/raw/final encoding |

impossible. The store exception is narrow: inspect borrowed stored bytes, charge,
then materialize; an exhausted heap never starts the decode/copy. SQLite borrows
its JSON text instead of first allocating a String. PostgreSQL preflights byte
lengths in its existing repeatable-read/serializable transaction. The measured
heap column describes these allowances; this ledger, not observations, is the bound.

## 2026-09-19 — W14A-FIX-2: prepay SQLite's resident preflight scratch

Closed the two remaining recheck findings against
`760bb0d1ac9d07e0e9a5ab9f946656f53089f794`. The High now reserves
`2 * page_size` once per read, before the first SQLite length preflight executes.
Each store connection reads its actual `PRAGMA page_size` once at open, including
independent and inspection readers; transactions carry that number. The keyed
meter allowance uses one inline bit, marks admission only after the heap charge
succeeds, and rolls back with its charge in a meter mark. Its unit test covers
1,000 repeated reservations, cap and abort, failed admission, fresh reads and
restoring marks both before and after payment. The actual-length allowance
before the subsequent payload statement is unchanged. The additional meter
state compiles only with SQLite. The Low changes the always-lazy comment's
reference from LLP 3000.007 §18.1 to §20.24.1, without changing traversal.

Correction to the earlier preflight descriptions: the length preflight is not
payload-free. In the bundled `libsqlite3-sys-0.38.2/sqlite3/sqlite3.c`, SQLite
3.53.2's `OP_Column` page-resident branch (lines 99667–99693) handles both TEXT
and BLOB without consulting P5: `szMalloc < len+2` guards `sqlite3VdbeMemGrow`,
then `memcpy` copies the cell. The following overflow branch (99694–99726)
consults `OPFLAG_BYTELENARG` / `LENGTHARG` and skips reading those payloads.
The two resident column registers are bounded by the page size and prepaid once
per read, not once per row, lane or fetch. The store comment, ledger and
§20.24.1 now say this. Cached VM/database images remain a separate shared class;
Rust still borrows the later JSON before decoding it.

scratch, so the probe also reports the JSON column's rounded `len+2` allocation,
statement runs and retained statement bytes. The resident row serializes to
720 bytes; the overflow row to 4,070 bytes. With a 500-byte allowance before
the fix, both preflights ran once: resident Rust/native/payload allocation was
320/1,976/728 bytes; overflow was 320/5,360/0. The regression summary was

## 2026-09-20 — W14A-FIX-3: charge each SQLite preflight row before stepping again

Closed the remaining cumulative-allocation finding against
`cddf0d42d67e474dea6b1589b451e0e0448b0fc7`. The SQLite size preflight now
streams `octet_length(r.data) + length(i.k)` in the scan's order, with the same
bounds and limit, and charges each row's `2 * length + 64` before stepping to
the next row. A refusal resets the statement without another step. The
once-per-read `2 * page_size` reserve remains, and the subsequent payload
statement uses the allowances already granted without charging them again.
The store comment, allocation ledger and LLP 3000.007 §20.24.1 record the
ordering exception: within one execution the first row's resident copy (one
page-size buffer per column, two registers) precedes its charge; every later
row's copy follows the previous row's charge. Across executions the reserve
prepays the first execution's first copy once per read, while later executions'
first copies are charged immediately after, bounded by the same constant.
Nothing else is copied before its allowance; overflow payloads are never read
by the length preflight.

Verified both bundled SQLite 3.53.2 facts in
`libsqlite3-sys-0.38.2/sqlite3/sqlite3.c`: the resident `OP_Column` branch tests
`pDest->szMalloc < len+2` at line 99681 and calls
`sqlite3VdbeMemGrow(pDest, len+2, 0)` at 99684. With preservation false,
lines 85764–85765 free the old allocation and allocate the entire new size.
`sqlite3_reset` calls `sqlite3VdbeReset` at 93694; a still-running VM is halted
at 91347, `sqlite3VdbeHalt` calls `closeAllCursors` at 91088, and that releases
the register array at 90597. Lines 89962–89963 free `zMalloc` and zero
`szMalloc`. Cached statements therefore allocate register buffers afresh on
each execution. The previous entry's once-per-read reserve bounds the first
copy, not a whole batch's cumulative allocation.

The regression uses 22 resident rows with body lengths `650 + 8*n` for
`n = 0..21`, `limit = 22`, a 9,000-byte heap ceiling and disabled lookaside.
The first attempt exposed host allocator slack: forwarding `xSize` unchanged
let two buffers cover all 22 lengths (2,752 native bytes, 1,504 payload bytes),
so it did not exercise every growth. The test-only forwarding allocator now
keeps an eight-byte size header and reports requested capacity rather than
platform `malloc_size` slack. Every eight-byte growth reaches `MemGrow`; native
totals count bytes requested from malloc/realloc, including those headers.
Production SQLite configuration is unchanged.

Red before the fix: native 19,368 B, payload 17,864 B, Rust 320 B; successfully
charged 8,297 B plus the 8,192 B ordering allowance gives a 16,489 B bound.
The native-allocation assertion fails, before checking the attempted charge
of 46,269 B. `Meter.used` includes the refused attempt, which is not an
allocation allowance. The isolated regression summary was
`test result: FAILED. 0 passed; 1 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 9 filtered out; finished in 0.01s`.
The brief's 17,952 B sum is corrected by this fixture: serialized JSON is
720–888 B and the 22 rounded payload requests are 728, 736, …, 896 B, summing
to 17,864 B. This still exceeds the bound and reproduces the High.

Green after the fix: native 1,768 B, payload 728 B, Rust 272 B, successfully
charged 8,297 B. The first row attempts 9,855 B, exceeds 9,000 B and refuses;
no second preflight row or payload fetch is copied. With ample headroom all
22 rows return in order with their original body lengths: native 38,144 B,
Rust 35,874 B, charged 137,863 B. The resident/overflow single-row and actual
page-size probes remain. Repeated fetches now count native allocations too:
resident first/next/fresh-read native bytes are 3,536/3,536/3,536, and overflow
14,400/14,400/14,400. The two-fetch native totals are 7,072 and 28,800 B;
their first/next/fresh-read meter charges remain 13,578/5,386/13,578 and
33,678/25,486/33,678 B. The tests check per-fetch and cumulative allowances
and that reset causes fresh payload allocations.

What I learned: a bound on live register capacity is not a bound on cumulative
allocation, and platform allocator slack can hide the repeated-growth case
unless the probe controls reported capacity. Admission must happen between
SQLite steps. No authoring form or diagnostic changes, so the README and guide
cards are unchanged. No ceiling, serialized form, cursor version, veto,
acquisition boundary, client runtime, existing corpus case, wasm budget or

## 2026-09-20 — W14A-FIX-4: pin SQLite execution storage outside the payload ledger

Base: `ab52240718e7f23b670b676be1d284b82e32f018`. Read both round-4 reviews:
GPT's remaining High is the cumulative native allocation of repeated empty
scans; Grok found no remaining payload-preflight defect. This implements the
lead's scope ruling under the author's sign-off, recorded in LLP 3000.007
§20.24.1: the ledger prices interpreter allocations and store payload copies
(row images, keys and resident-payload registers), with the existing preflight
ordering exception. The storage engine's per-execution statement storage and
page cache are shared images outside it. Execution storage is transient and
freed at reset; it is measured and pinned, not charged. Every store scan has
this exclusion; pricing it only for word reads would make their costs
incomparable with the engine's other reads. No production executable text or
charge changes; the ledger and store edits are comments only.

Extended the existing lookaside-disabled native allocator probe to count
successful allocations, frees and peak live requested capacity, including its
existing size headers. Realloc conservatively counts the new buffer before
subtracting the old one. All existing probe assertions remain byte-identical.
The new test warms both statements, proves the empty range is valid, uses
`limit = 1`, checks both statement execution counts, and tests one scan and
1,000 scans sharing one meter. Every scan succeeds with an empty result and
no cap. After every scan, allocations minus frees is zero.

| Scans | Statement executions | Native allocated B | Native B/scan (mean / max) | Peak live B | Native freed B | End live B | Meter heap B |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 2 | 1,952 | 1,952 / 1,952 | 976 | 1,952 | 0 | 8,297 |
| 1,000 | 2,000 | 1,952,000 | 1,952 / 1,952 | 976 | 1,952,000 | 0 | 113,192 |

`PIN = 2,048 B` rounds the measured pair of executions, 1,952 B, up to the
next 1,024 B. Each scan must allocate at most PIN, and the whole measured
run's peak live must stay at most `2 * PIN = 4,096 B`. The meter remains
`8,192 + 105 * scans`: the once-per-read reserve plus each scan's range/names.
The warmed page cache is outside the measurement; these are requested
capacities, not platform allocator slack or RSS. The result demonstrates why
cumulative allocation and live storage cannot be interchanged in this scope
ruling: native allocation grows with scan count while live execution storage
returns to zero after every reset pair.

Before changing the contract prose, the new measurement ran with the old
unscoped assertion `native as u64 <= meter.used.heap_bytes + 2 * page_size`.
It failed at 1,000 scans: 1,952,000 native B exceeds 121,384 B allowed by that
claim. Command (from `snapback4/`, Node 24 on PATH and `CARGO_NET_OFFLINE=true`):
`cargo test -p snapback4-core --test word_heap sqlite_empty_scan_statement_storage_is_pinned_and_transient -- --exact --nocapture`.
Red: `test result: FAILED. 0 passed; 1 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 10 filtered out; finished in 0.01s`.
With that rejected assertion removed and the ruled per-scan/peak-live pins
retained, the same command is green:
`test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 10 filtered out; finished in 0.00s`.
This is a counterexample to the old scope claim, not a red-to-green production
fix: production charges are identical, and the final contract test passes on
that unchanged behavior.

## 2026-09-22 — 0.3 program: generation discovery before a sync page is materialized (LLP 3000.007 ruling 48)

A `/sync` request can now carry the device's `generation`. When it differs,
the server answers HTTP 200 `E_SYNC_GENERATION` before it builds any snapshot
or stream page. The answer carries the generation, the store id and the
current numeric head. The client adopts only when that head is a finite,
nonnegative integer at or above its retained image-head evidence. A lower
head halts with `E_STORE_RESTORE`, and a missing head is a retryable failure
that keeps the evidence. Clients that send no generation see unchanged
behavior. A new client against 0.2.32, which denies unknown fields, retries
once without the field and latches that origin only after the stripped retry
succeeds.

MC1's gate 5 was re-measured with its own fixture, unchanged. A lagging device
now gets a 234-byte generation refusal, adopts, and reacquires with no
oversized response (`snapback4/reports/20260922-sync-generation.md`).
Maintained columns are unblocked. `serve.rs`'s sync handling moved to
`serve_sync.rs` to stay under the file cap.

## 2026-09-22 — 0.3 program: the declared Following timeline, server side (F3a; LLP 3000.007.003 §3.3)

`maintain feed: timeline` maps the application's profiles, posts (with a
one-way `removed` flag), reposts and follows. The feeds recipe's projection
tables become **engine-owned**:

- author modes, pull routes, slot counts and the route total;
- events, tombstones, private inboxes and broadcasts.

The engine runs the recipe's logic on each actual transition, inside the
writing mutation's transaction and meter, through the ordinary validation,
constraint, cap and index path. A scoped, restoring authority lets it write
only those tables. The oracle is recipe-trace equivalence against the
installed recipe and its generated bridge. It has two documented
exceptions:

- F3 keeps no duplicate follow-edge table, so a maximum-backfill promotion
  is 1,023 writes against the recipe's 1,024;
- F3 refuses a caller-chosen event id equal to a tombstoned event's id.

Implemented by an Astra xhigh lane on the black M5 Max. It stopped twice
with counterexamples that became RFC revisions:

- **Revision 5:** the recipe's duplicate follow edge.
- **Revision 6:** lazy author registration broke "never refuse what the
  recipe admits" at the write ceiling, so authors register eagerly.

Three review rounds followed:

- **Round 1** (Astra NOT READY; Grok NOT READY on 11 of 19 packets). Owned
  rows took caller-supplied ids, so a later collision could probe another
  reader's private inbox. Owned rows now take SHA-256 digest ids of their
  natural keys (revision 7); natural-key ids alone exceeded the 144-byte
  identity limit, and the lane stopped on that as well. The purge job's
  authority was ambient; redefinition compared a physical index; and
  namespaces, admission and panics needed hardening.
- **Round 2** (Astra NOT READY; Grok mixed). A repost could reuse a removed
  event's id and collide with a copy still awaiting purge, so every new
  event now refuses while its id is tombstoned. Authority is checked on every
  write path, an upsert needs both grants, and core validation re-derives
  the stored sets.
- **Round 3:** Astra READY with no findings, including no remaining caller
  path to place or probe an owned private row. Grok's remaining items were
  test strength; the purge-atomicity regression moves to F3b's fix round.

It landed after a rebase onto `556a86216`. Three conflicts were additive:
the `use server` and timeline binder hooks, the language card's schedule
count, and the serve test modules. On the rebased tree, `scripts/test.sh` reported `== 0 failure(s) in 672 s` on the M5. The main commits after the rebase base touched no Snapback 4 code.

Wasm is 449,347 B gzip on the lane's base, within the 452,000 budget. F3b
raises the budget.

## 2026-09-23 — 0.3 program: the declared timeline on devices (F3b) and its sizing (F3c)

**F3b (devices).** Posting, reposting, removal and profile registration run
in the device's provisional transaction, sharing one implementation with the
server. They predict only when every input is held and covered. Retained
history never counts: point hits, point misses, scans and empty ranges all
check coverage by the actual key, and a retained input queues the whole
mutation. Follow and unfollow always queue, because slot accounting reads
online-only counts. Owned rows take the same digest ids on every host.

Prediction writes no owned row the predictor's read rule denies. A
one-follower post therefore predicts three rows on the author's device
(post, event, own copy). The recipe's witness also predicted the follower's
copy, which was locally readable by the author. The general gap in the
device read path is
`issues/20260922-snapback4-device-reads-trust-predicted-rows.md`, owned by
the program lead and due before 0.3.0.

Deliverability follows LLP 3000.007.003 revision 7. `check --cost` bounds
each operation's derived stream bytes; the largest, a maximum-backfill
promotion, is 888,757 B. SDK clients on WASM and native SQLite, left behind a
timeline commit that grew past the ceiling, recover through the snapshot
restart with pending writes intact.

**F3c (sizing).** `size authors N, edges N` has the recipe's semantics
(`init --recipe feeds --authors N --edges N`), so the declaration holds the
Clique fixture's 1,008 authors and 5,921 edges. The recipe-trace oracle runs
at both sizes.

**Lanes and reviews.** Both were Astra xhigh lanes on the black M5 Max. F3b
first stopped on a real counterexample: the stream re-reads current row
images into old commits, which led to revision 7.

- **F3b round 1:** Astra NOT READY. Its High, found under the partition
  focus, was that a predicted foreign inbox copy was readable by its author.
- **F3b round 2:** Astra NOT READY; retained absence justified a
  prediction.
- **F3b round 3:** Astra READY, with no findings.
- **F3c:** Astra READY WITH CHANGES (one docs wording, fixed at landing);
  Grok READY or READY WITH CHANGES on all packets.

An independent Astra review of the program then found that the published
0.2.33 device silently accepts a timeline backend and mispredicts. It
predicts only the post, and Following comes back empty but marked complete.
A shared capability fence (lane FENCE) must land before 0.3.0.

## 2026-09-23 — 0.3 program: the device authorizes provisional rows at read time (READAUTH)

Device reads trust every row in a synced table, because a delivered row was
authorized by the server. A predicted row was not. A mutation whose writes
produced a row its writer cannot read left that row readable until
settlement (`issues/20260922-snapback4-device-reads-trust-predicted-rows.md`;
owned by the program lead and due before 0.3.0). An independent Astra review
of the program asked for this shared correction.

**The mechanism.** A device read that touches a provisional row evaluates the
table's read rule for the device's principal against the combined pending
state.

- Rule witnesses are raw, as on the server: the device's own pending writes
  count as present, and delivered witnesses only when covered. A
  retained-only witness is unknown, and unknown hides the row.
- The verdict is three-way (readable, denied, unknown), evaluated once per
  read. Meter exhaustion stays a meter cut.
- This covers point reads, scans, merges, pages, counts, probes,
  prediction's own reads and watches.
- Delivered rows keep their trust. Mutations still predict; unreadable
  provisional rows are simply invisible until settlement. The declared
  timeline keeps its foreign-row skip.

**Three review rounds.**

- **v1 checked at prediction time and queued.** Astra NOT READY, with three
  Highs that a prediction-time check cannot close: a retained grant
  authorized a prediction, a later pending mutation revoked an earlier
  prediction's authority, and old provisional rows survived an upgrade. The
  mechanism moved to read time.
- **v2** closed those three. Astra NOT READY on recursive witness
  authorization: service-seat disjuncts were hidden and a meter cut was
  erased. Witnesses became raw.
- **The final round** closed those. Astra found no disclosure or format
  regression. Its two remaining Mediums, both over-refusal or over-hiding
  edge cases, are batched with F2's in
  `issues/20260923-snapback4-readauth-and-f2-edge-cases.md` for a lane
  before 0.3.0.

Integrated suite on the M5: `== 1 failure(s) in 644 s`. The client failures
were an Expo media-migration test and a session-restore test. Both pass when
